summary: Zakah al-Fitr (also called Sadaqat al-Fitr) is a charitable obligation due at the end of Ramadan before the Eid al-Fitr prayer. It purifies the fasting person of any deficiencies in their fast and provides food for the poor on the day of Eid.
content:
## Definition and Status

Zakah al-Fitr is an obligatory (wajib) amount of food given in charity by every Muslim at the end of Ramadan before the Eid prayer. It differs from regular zakah in that it is attached to the person (not accumulated wealth) and is due annually at a specific time.

Ibn Umar (رضي الله عنه) narrated: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made zakah al-fitr obligatory upon the Muslims — a sa' of dates or a sa' of barley — upon every free person and slave, male and female, young and old among the Muslims. He commanded that it be paid before the people go out to the prayer." (Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1503; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 984)

## Purpose

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ enjoined zakah al-fitr to purify the fasting person from indecent words and actions, and to provide food for the indigent." (Sunan Abu Dawud, Hadith 1609; graded hasan sahih by many scholars)

Thus zakah al-fitr serves two purposes: spiritual purification of the faster's Ramadan, and ensuring that the poor have food to celebrate Eid.

## Amount

All four schools agree the amount is one sa' per person (the sa' is an ancient volumetric measure).

**Modern equivalents:** One sa' is approximately 2.5 to 3 kilograms, or roughly four mudd (handfuls). The exact gram equivalent varies by the food type and by scholarly calculation. Contemporary Islamic organizations typically cite 2.5 kg–3 kg as the standard amount.

**Exception — Hanafi position on wheat:** The Hanafi school holds that wheat (and flour and bread) requires only half a sa' (approximately 1.75 kg), as half a sa' of wheat was considered equivalent in value to a full sa' of dates or barley in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. Other schools do not accept this reduction and require a full sa' regardless of the grain type.

## Food Types

The authentic hadith specify: dates, barley, raisins, dried curd (aqit), and wheat. (Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1506; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 985)

**Can money substitute for food?**

**Hanafi:** Yes. Paying the monetary equivalent is permissible and may even be preferable in some circumstances because money allows the poor to buy what they actually need.

**Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali:** No. Zakah al-Fitr must be paid in food. The texts specify food types, and giving money is a deviation from the Sunnah that is not permitted. This is the position of most classical scholars.

Note: This is a well-known and significant difference with practical implications. Contemporary Muslims often follow the Hanafi position for convenience. Those who follow the non-Hanafi schools should give food or ensure that their zakah organization distributes actual food, not cash equivalents.

## Who Must Pay

**Hanafi:** Zakah al-Fitr is obligatory upon a Muslim who:
- Owns the equivalent of the nisab (the same threshold as regular zakah) beyond their basic needs on the day of Eid
- Pays on behalf of themselves and their minor children who do not own nisab themselves
- Does not pay on behalf of adult children, wives, or adult dependents unless they voluntarily do so

**Maliki:** Obligatory upon a Muslim who has food beyond their needs for that day and night. Pays on behalf of oneself and all dependents under one's financial responsibility (minor children, wife, and in some views poor adult children and parents).

**Shafi'i:** Obligatory upon one who has food beyond their needs for Eid day and night. Pays on behalf of all dependents including wife and all minor children. If one's wife has her own wealth, she pays for herself.

**Hanbali:** Obligatory upon one with sufficient means. Pays on behalf of all financial dependents including wife, minor children, and — in the school's view — those servants one is responsible for.

## On Behalf of Others

All schools agree a Muslim may pay zakah al-fitr on behalf of themselves and their minor children. The obligation or permission to pay on behalf of others (wife, adult children, servants, elderly parents) varies as described above.

The Prophet ﷺ commanded zakah al-fitr for "every free person and slave, male and female, young and old" — indicating broad coverage including those who cannot earn for themselves.

## Timing

Zakah al-Fitr has three time windows:

1. **Permissible early:** Two days before Eid per the Shafi'i school (Ibn Umar's practice); one to two days before per Maliki; the Hanafi school permits paying throughout Ramadan; the Hanbali permits paying from the beginning of Ramadan.

2. **Recommended:** Before the Eid prayer — all schools agree this is the optimal time, as the hadith explicitly commands it before going out to prayer.

3. **Valid but disliked:** After the Eid prayer until sunset per the Maliki and Shafi'i schools. The Hanafi school allows it to be paid even later without sin.

4. **Sin:** Delaying past Eid Day without excuse — the majority consider this a sin. The Hanafi school considers it a qada' obligation that must still be fulfilled.

## Recipients

Zakah al-Fitr is given to the same eight categories as regular zakah (Surah al-Tawbah, 9:60), with priority given to the poor and needy so they may celebrate Eid without worry.

Concentrating it on one or two categories (especially the poor and needy) is permissible and often the practice of zakah organizations. It is given preferentially to Muslims in the local community, though — as with regular zakah — there is scholarly discussion on whether it can be transferred to Muslims in other regions when local need is less.
evidence_hadith: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1503; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 984 — Ibn Umar narration on zakah al-fitr obligation and timing
Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1506; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 985 — food types for zakah al-fitr
Sunan Abu Dawud, Hadith 1609 — purpose: purification of the fast and feeding the poor (hasan sahih)

madhab_positions.hanafi: Half a sa' of wheat is sufficient (other grains: one sa'). Monetary payment is permissible. Obligatory only upon one who owns nisab. Pays on behalf of oneself and minor children only. Can be paid anytime during Ramadan.
madhab_positions.maliki: Full sa' of food required (no monetary substitute). Obligatory on one who has food beyond Eid day and night's needs. Pays for all financial dependents including wife. Preferred: day of Eid before prayer.
madhab_positions.shafii: Full sa' required. No monetary substitute. Obligatory upon one with food beyond day's needs. Pays for all dependents including wife (unless she has her own wealth). Permissible to pay two days before Eid.
madhab_positions.hanbali: Full sa' required. No monetary substitute. Obligatory on those with means. Pays for all dependents. Permissible from start of Ramadan. Recommended before Eid prayer.
